title: Apollo Client
description: Comprehensive GraphQL client with caching and state management.

data.text: Apollo Client is a full-featured GraphQL client with intelligent caching, optimistic UI, and dev tools.

data.title: Apollo Client setup

data.text: The Normalized Cache Is the Point

Apollo Client keeps a normalized store keyed by object type and id, so if two components query the same user, it is stored once and both read from cache. Queries declare the fields they need; the cache serves whatever is already available and fetches the rest.

data.title: A typed query hook

data.text: A mutation can update the cache directly so the UI reflects the change without a refetch. `update` rewrites the cache, `refetchQueries` re-runs named queries, and `optimisticResponse` shows the result before the server replies. This is how Apollo avoids stale lists after a create.

data.title: A mutation that updates the cached list
Interview angle: cache policies and staleness
data.text: The trade-off with Apollo is staleness: the cache can show data that the server has since changed. `fetchPolicy` controls this — `cache-first`, `network-only`, `cache-and-network`, `no-cache` — and the right choice depends on how fresh the screen must be. Interviewers want to hear that a normalized cache saves requests but can serve stale data unless you invalidate it.
